# ravenna_ticket_status (Resource)

A ticket status. Every status belongs to a status group, which Ravenna manages — use the `ravenna_status_group` data source to resolve one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "ravenna_status_group" "pending" {
  label = "Pending"
}

resource "ravenna_ticket_status" "waiting_on_vendor" {
  label           = "Waiting on vendor"
  status_group_id = data.ravenna_status_group.pending.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `label` (String) Status label shown on tickets.
- `status_group_id` (String) Status group this status belongs to. Changing it forces a new status, because the API accepts the group only at creation.

### Optional

- `delete_target_status_id` (String) Status to move this status's tickets onto when it is destroyed. Only used on destroy, and Terraform destroys with the value already in state, so apply a change to this attribute before destroying the status. Not read back from the API; an imported status shows it as null.
- `order` (Number) Display order within the status group.
- `request_type_id` (String) Restrict the status to a single request type. Write-only: the Ravenna API accepts this at creation but does not return it as a scalar, so Terraform cannot detect drift on it and an imported status will show it as null. Changing this forces a new status.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Status identifier.
- `system` (Boolean) Whether Ravenna manages this status as a system status.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Note: request_type_id is write-only — the Ravenna API does not return
# it as a scalar, so an imported status shows it as null.
terraform import ravenna_ticket_status.waiting_on_vendor s_01HXYZ
```
